headline.caveat: US government took ~10% (9.9%) of Intel common stock at $20.47/share by converting $5.7B of unpaid CHIPS Act grants plus $3.2B of Secure Enclave awards — grants became equity, not new appropriations.

realized_to_date.caveat: $5.7B of previously-awarded-but-unpaid CHIPS funds were funded around close; the $3.2B Secure Enclave component pays against program milestones. Exact cumulative funding not publicly reconciled.

nature_md: The US government converted Intel's outstanding CHIPS Act awards ($5.7B unpaid grants) and $3.2B Secure Enclave program funding into ~433M shares (~9.9%) of Intel common stock at $20.47/share — turning subsidy into state shareholding. The stake is passive (no board seat, agreed voting alignment with the board), and includes a 5-year warrant for an additional ~5% at $20/share exercisable only if Intel ceases to own at least 51% of its foundry business. Precedent-setting: grants-for-equity replaced milestone grants as US industrial policy's instrument of choice.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: For the government: no new cash beyond already-appropriated CHIPS/Secure Enclave funds; the Treasury holds equity whose value floats with INTC. Not a procurement contract — no goods received.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Intel receives the cash as equity issuance (balance sheet: cash up, equity up) rather than deferred grant income tied to capex milestones — cleaner and faster than CHIPS disbursement, at the cost of ~10% dilution plus warrant overhang.

both_sides_md: **Bull:** anchors Intel's foundry ambitions with the state's balance sheet and aligns Washington with Intel's survival — 13F filings later marked the stake around $9.5B. **Bear:** dilutive, politicizes capital allocation, and the foundry-ownership warrant condition constrains strategic options (a foundry spin-off would trigger further dilution); press-vs-filing value discrepancies flagged in tracker data-quality notes.

events.title: Intel and US government agree $8.9B equity conversion of CHIPS grants
